findings.claim: G2's set test fails every correct build as written, so W2 is not met. Section 6.1 G2 (2) (line 619) builds the LIVE SIDE from p's intents 'of every status'. The shadow writes one intent per candidate and marks an issuer it held in the last 5 sessions `skipped:issuer-held` (rel/1019h programs.py write_intents, _held_recently). The HISTORY SIDE (G2 (3), lines 620-623, and section 3.5 line 434) applies p's one-position rule from the export's intents, as book.picks/held_recently do, so it never holds those pairs. d/u then equals the share of held pairs, far above 0.10 x u + 2. The same gap breaks the 0.05 containment test for DROP/UNDER. Under the 'less likely to pass / trades less' ambiguity rule (7.6.13, section 17) a coder takes this reading. g2_w9.py never models the one-position mechanics: its 'correct build' is the same set less a mapping noise m. So the 0.99-1.00 figure in sections 0 and 11.6 is not evidence for the rule as written.
findings.evidence: evl9/recheck2/rc2_held.py -> rc2_held.out (the lens generator's own issuer law: 3,000 issuers, Zipf(0.8), 5-session hold). The share of a control's pairs that are skipped:issuer-held is 0.176 / 0.239 / 0.335 / 0.415 / 0.435 / 0.530 at 25 / 60 / 135 / 250 / 300 / 515 names a session. The controls shadow 135-550 intents a session (SPEED-FACTS). Code: evl9/recheck2/code/programs.py lines 765-812 and book.py lines 957-969 and 1006-1059.
findings.fix: G2 (2): the live side is p's intents of each overlap session, every status EXCEPT those written at decision as `skipped:issuer-held` or `skipped:no-exit-session`; later moves such as skipped:no-auction, excluded, taken or limit are kept. G2 (3): the twin's one-position state is the export's NON-SKIPPED intents of p, read as programs._held_recently reads them, A72's 'ahead' reading included. Add to (4)'s stated skews the pairs whose live and point-in-time eligible SYMBOL differ, for example multi-class names. Extend g2_w9.py with the shadow's one-position mechanics: Zipf repeats, a 5-session hold, live intents carrying held statuses. Show the fixed rule passing >= 0.99 and the 'every status' reading failing, and restate the section 0 and 11.6 figures from that run.

findings.claim: The integration files are pinned as WHOLE FILES, which leaves no workable reading. Section 6.2 (lines 669-670) requires the release to carry run.py, book.py, programs.py and screen.py 'byte-identical to their pinned sha256'. Section 1.3 (lines 193-195) makes any change to 'an integration file of section 7.6' a NEW VERSION with its own charge. Item 7.6.12 (lines 839-843) says a change before the first live decision merely restarts the record. Section 9 (line 901) admits receipts of 'the release carrying the pinned code ... or a later one'. Those four files change in nearly every House release: 1019i carries PREREG-EVL-6's and -7's code in them, and PREREG-EVL-8's code comes next. So either the lane cannot ship, or every release re-versions both learners at 2 x 0.13 each against a LEFT of 0.78. Three readings exist, and the strict one is unworkable.
findings.evidence: PREREG-EVL-9.md 6.2, 1.3, 7.6 item 12, 9. A116 and A117 put EVL-6/7 code (feat/evl-6, feat/evl-7) and infra in release 1019i, then EVL-8's code, all touching run.py, book.py and screen.py. On rel/1019h book.py alone hosts allocation, sizing, guards and picks for every program.
findings.fix: Pin the integration as code, not file bytes. (a) Every line of the warm integration lives in league/events/warm/ and is pinned byte-identical: the hook body, the warm_stats writer, the POOL control builder and the book-row ordering function. (b) The call sites in run.py, book.py, programs.py and screen.py are named, one function each, and pinned by the sha256 of that function's source (ast.get_source_segment), with the receipt carrying those hashes. (c) A GOLDEN FIXTURE test fixed at CODE_PIN_9 must pass byte for byte on every later release: decide() outputs, ROOM order with this file's ids, the POOL control's values. (d) Only a change to a pinned function or a golden failure is a new version (1.3); other edits in those files are not. Reconcile 6.2, 1.3, 7.6.12 and 9's 'or a later one' to this one rule.

findings.claim: File modes cannot deliver the no-abandon guarantee on this machine, and the free-VOID window contains labels. blake-desktop has passwordless sudo for the owner's account, which every agent session uses, so mode-0700 ltcm-warm trees and the unit's private tmpfs are readable by any person or agent. The lines 'no person's account reads them' (1.1 step 3, lines 145-148) and 'No person can read a fitted model before its hash is public' (0, 13) are therefore policy, not mechanism. Worse, step c computes labels (LABEL_SHA, G1's coverage) BEFORE TRAIN-START, and until TRAIN-START the version VOIDs free: by a gate failure, or by the 5-session deadline lapse (1.2 (iii)). Someone can read the labels, fit privately, stop the job, and let it lapse free. That is the option W4 closes. Two further gaps: the captain makes the G2 export, and its timing against the labels is not pinned. The export lands in the 0330 drop dir as a captain-owned, captain-readable file, despite 'not readable by the captain's account' (B7, lines 696-698). After TRAIN-START a G4/G5 failure is still a free VOID, so tampering with the second training run buys a free exit.
findings.evidence: ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md: 'Passwordless sudo is enabled.' PREREG-EVL-9.md 1.1 steps 3b-3d (labels in the canonical tables before TRAIN-START), 1.2 (i)-(iii), B7.
findings.fix: (1) The job pushes a FETCH-START commit BEFORE its first price-bearing request. It names the code tag, the price-free RAW_SHA and the sha256 of the G2 export, which must already be in the drop dir. The job refuses any other export. (2) From FETCH-START on there is no deadline VOID: a lapse draws 2 x c9. The only VOID is a gate failure the job pushes itself, carrying its inputs' hashes so anyone with the vault can recompute it. G4/G5 failures after TRAIN-START also draw. (3) Replace the mode-based claims with the honest guarantee: root (the owner's account via passwordless sudo) can read the vault and the tmpfs. What protects the record is the public FETCH-START/TRAIN-START draw plus section 1.4's recorded reads.

findings.claim: W11's timing table (7.3, lines 757-780) is stale against PREREG-EVL-8's newest text (sha256 ea1173a9, revised after its re-check 2) and against rel/1019h's cadence. (a) The event book plans once a minute, 3 s past the minute. The last close tick inside the window is 15:48:03 and the 15:49 tick is past close_until. 'Real money buys only intents written by 15:48:40' therefore cannot be implemented: an intent written at 15:48:10-15:48:40 is never planned. The true condition is EVL-WL-ON's intents written before the 15:48 tick, meaning the lane's close receipt by about 15:47:38 (META's full 15 s plus 10 s) or 15:47:53. PREREG-EVL-5's part at its bound (45 s plus 15 s) alone exceeds that, so the stated 75/90 s and the real-money coverage are wrong. (b) The prepasses (120 s, 'lowest priority') lack EVL-8's YIELD rule, so on the lane's single task slot they can delay a verdict or record pass due before 09:15 or 15:46. Those answers feed earlier rows' real-money picks, which breaks 'without delaying them'. (c) The warm parts' priority after the receipt is not stated: EVL-8 makes its own run the first task after the receipt, and a verdict or record pass could run before decide-close-warm9.
findings.evidence: evl8/PREREG-EVL-8.md section 4.6 (newest): 'THE BOOK makes ONE DECISION AN AUCTION at its minute tick (live/step.py: MINUTE_OFFSET 3 s)... The last tick inside the close window is the 15:48 tick (15:48:03 or later); the 15:49 tick is past the cut-off'. Prepasses 'YIELD before each step'. decide-*-px8 and meta8 are 'THE FIRST TASK THE LANE RUNS AFTER THE RECEIPT'. rel/1019h league/live/step.py MINUTE_OFFSET = 3.0. evl9/final/timing9.py hard-codes EVL-8's superseded table.
findings.fix: Rebuild 7.3 and timing9.py on PREREG-EVL-8's final table. Both prepasses yield before each step to any lane task due and write nothing until whole. decide-open-warm9 and decide-close-warm9 are the next task after EVL-8's run, or after the lane's first ok/pending receipt when EVL-8 has none, ahead of any record or verdict pass due. The open late pass is at the first book tick after decide-open-warm9 finishes. Real money at the close only for intents written before the 15:48 tick, in the close late pass after EVL-8's. Restate the coverage condition and the timing9.out figures. Add tests with the lane receipt at 15:47:30 (planned) and 15:47:55 (not planned), and with a verdict pass due during a prepass.

findings.claim: G2's feature test can VOID a correct builder through data vintage. G2 (6) (lines 633-639) compares raw columns at 1e-9 relative, but the live side reads the House's bars and universe row, fetched at its decisions, while the history side reads the vault's bars, fetched days later after CODE_PIN_9. Section 12 itself names 'late-print restatements in daily bars'. ln(adv20) sums 20 close-times-volume products, so a single revised volume on any of 20 days changes it beyond 1e-9. sig20, ln(prev_close), bench_iwm and dmove are exposed the same way. A modest revision rate pushes a column past 0.05 x pairs + 2. That tests the data's vintage, not the builder, and a VOID costs a night and a re-registration.
findings.evidence: PREREG-EVL-9.md G2 (6), section 12 row 1 residual. g2_w9.py draws feature mismatches at m/4 only and has no bar-vintage term.
findings.fix: Compute G2's feature comparison from the EXPORT's bars and marks on both sides, so it tests the builder. Test the vault's bars against the export's separately: raw closes within 1e-9 on >= 99% of name-days, volumes within 1e-3 relative on >= 95%. Remove the differing name-days' pairs as a stated skew counted in the receipt.

findings.claim: Forward-row reads are not as-of the live decision. warm_stats and warm_cands have no write time. A warm_stats row held for the 2-session wait (7.1) and written late with settled_by < tau enters every later reading of a decision but not the live one, so the recompute alarms and the money is held. first20 reads KEPT sets that a late or catch-up decision writes after tau. The 7.6.1 identity test ('delete every row stored at or after tau') cannot identify such rows.
findings.evidence: PREREG-EVL-9.md 7.1, 7.2 ('a row's write time never decides'), 7.4 table columns, 7.6 item 1, item 5 first20.
findings.fix: Add written_at to warm_stats and warm_cands. The live decision and its nightly recompute admit only rows written before tau with settled_by before tau. The catch-up and the reconstruction (training state) read by settled_by as now. first20 reads KEPT sets written before tau.

findings.claim: Budget and deadline gaps. (a) CODE_PIN_9 has no deadline, so the 0.26 reserved at T_F can block the budget indefinitely. (b) On rel/1019h R3's validator counts SEATING only (programs in code), so births between T_F and B6's release do not see the reservation. (c) The receipt deadline equals the TRAIN-START deadline (the 5th session after CODE_PIN_9), so a job started on night 5 lapses into a draw. (d) Section 9's 'where the two differ, PREREG-EVL-6 wins' contradicts its own RUNS bullet. That bullet says 'does not start ... never seats again'; EVL-6 section 3 says a version waiting for room stays in learning and starts its run when the budget holds it.
findings.evidence: rel/1019h league/events/births.py budget_used_tenths (SN.expected_false_passes over SEATING). PREREG-EVL-9.md 1.2, 9 (lines 896, 904-909), 10. Frozen EVL-6 section 3 'FRESH RUNS AND THE BUDGET'.
findings.fix: Make the file VOID, releasing the reservation, if CODE_PIN_9 is not tagged by a stated session after T_F. Enter the reservation in R3's count at T_F, via a registry or money row shipped before the first birth night after T_F, or check the T_M draw against LEFT. Give the receipt its own deadline counted from TRAIN-START. In section 9, say this file's stricter run-start rule binds (as PREREG-EVL-7 1.10), or adopt EVL-6's waiting rule.

findings.claim: Re-runs and probes can be implemented two ways. (a) A re-run when TRAIN-START or the receipt is already on GitHub is unpinned: a second TRAIN-START, a second receipt commit (which one is T_M?), or a person-pushed receipt whose model files were already deleted. Error responses are either re-fetched (which breaks determinism) or never re-fetched (permanent gaps). (b) B0's probes P2 (delisted bar coverage) and P3 (SPY bars) are v2/stocks/bars requests scheduled 'now', against 'No price-bearing request of section 3.1 is ever made before [CODE_PIN_9]' and 1.1 step 0.
findings.evidence: PREREG-EVL-9.md 1.1 steps 3a-3f, 1.2, 3.1 vault paragraph. evl9/scout/probe_counts.py p2_bars and P3 (v2/stocks/bars).
findings.fix: Status-200 responses are never re-fetched. Others are retried only inside step b, before FETCH-START. After TRAIN-START the vault is frozen: a re-run verifies its hashes equal TRAIN-START's (else it stops, no VOID), pushes no second TRAIN-START, and when the receipt is already on GitHub moves the reproduced model whose sha equals MODEL_SHA. T_M is the first receipt commit's landing. Run P2/P3 after CODE_PIN_9, or state their count-only exemption.

findings.claim: Rules a coder could still implement two ways (each small). (a) W1's condition covers dmove only; it should cover every own-price column EVL-7's frozen text drops or masks (items 7-8 too). (b) R* is chosen on the last 20% of sessions (2025-26) and reused by the forward-chained 2023-24 folds, against W6's 'never on later years'. (c) G2 reads 'the model file's META' at step c, before any model file exists. (d) B7's export omits `receipts`, needed for the eligibility cut and the overlap sessions, and does not pin --sessions. (e) G2b runs parse_form4 on the .txt, but it parses the ownershipDocument XML. Exact officer_title equality risks a free VOID. The joint-filing wording ('first reporting owner's rows; flags joined') does not match parse_form4's one row per owner. (f) Form 4 placeholders ('NONE', 'N/A' -> 'N.A') pass SYMBOL's regex. (g) It is unstated whether marks_read_at bounds book.picks' REACT/DROP/UNDER reaction marks too, and whether the reaction readers are store-only. (h) 7.6.4 'cut applied by decide': inside, via a cut universe, or on book.picks' output? (i) Item 5's 'live counts every stored article' ignores news_rows' live-flag rule. (j) A failed prepass leaves no SPY/IWM bars, so 'the part computes everything itself' is false and no candidate can pass sigH20. (k) The rate pauses in Z are EDT-only. (l) 3.6's ladder is not score.exit_ladder.
findings.evidence: PREREG-EVL-9.md 4 (W1 condition), 5.1, 6.1 G2 (6), B7, G2b, 3.4, 2.1, 7.6.4, item 5, 7.3 prepass row, 12 rate row, 3.6. rel/1019h edgar.parse_form4 (XML root; per-owner rows), book.reaction_reader (reads any stored '1530' mark, else fetches), score.exit_ladder (next 5 closes, then first trades).
findings.fix: (a) Drop any own-price column EVL-7's frozen text drops or masks. (b) Choose R* per fold inside its training eras. (c) Compute META in step c and write it unchanged into the model file. (d) Add receipts; --sessions = every lane session from 2026-10-19 decided before the export. (e) Extract the <XML> block; compare titles normalised (or ins_top's regex); form4_owners one row per owner. (f) Add a placeholder stop list; a conflicted rule (1) falls to rule (2). (g) Every '1530' read of a decision uses marks_read_at; the readers are store-only. (h) Apply the cut inside, via a universe restricted to results decided by the cut. (i) features() applies programs.news_rows' rule on both stores. (j) Without benchmark bars no candidate is eligible (fail closed, counted). (k) State the pauses in ET. (l) Call it this file's history ladder.
